problem:
From **left to right**, the ellipse ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+12x+4y=28$ intercepts the $x$-axis at the points $A$ and $B.$ Find the coordinates of these points.

$A($
{{field-1}}
$,$
{{field-2}}$)\,$

and 

$\,B($
{{field-3}}$,$
{{field-4}}$)\,$
worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercepts, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+12x+4y & =28 \\ {x}^{2}+(0)^{2}+12x+4(0) & =28 \\ {x}^{2}+12x & =28 \\ ({x}^{2}+12x+36)-36 & =28 \\ (x+6)^{2}-36 & =28 \\ (x+6)^{2} & =64 \\ x+6 & =\pm 8 \\ x & =-6\pm 8 \\ x & =-14,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are

$$
A(-14,0)\,\text{and}\,B(2,0).
$$
